# HAL-SHS - Sciences de l'Homme et de la Société

> HAL-SHS is France's open access digital archive for humanities and social sciences research, providing free access to scholarly publications across multiple disciplines.

HAL-SHS (Humanities and Social Sciences) is part of the broader HAL Open Archive initiative, serving as a multidisciplinary repository for academic research dissemination in France. The platform enables researchers to share and discover peer-reviewed articles, datasets, and scholarly works across archaeology, history, environmental studies, and related fields.

## Discovery & Search

- [Home - HAL-SHS](https://shs.hal.science): HAL-SHS homepage: open archive for humanities and social sciences research
- [Browse by Domain](https://shs.hal.science/browse/domain): Domain-based search interface for HAL Open Archive research collection
- [Browse by Period](https://shs.hal.science/browse/period): Period-based search interface for browsing HAL Open Archive by time
- [Browse by Document Type](https://shs.hal.science/browse/doctype): Document type search interface for browsing HAL Open Archive collections

## Featured Research

- [Xynthia: Lessons from a Catastrophe](https://shs.hal.science/hal-00613736v1): Analysis of 2010 Xynthia storm disaster in France by Etienne Chauveau
- [Forest Herding and Tree Foddering in Neolithic Europe](https://shs.hal.science/halshs-05560967v1): Neolithic herding practices studied via stable isotope analysis by Balasse et al.
- [Participatory Approaches and Archaeological Heritage at UNESCO](https://shs.hal.science/halshs-05556736v1): Comparative study of participatory archaeology in Roman fortifications by Goreau and Salin
- [Curated Datasets for Literary Tourism: Knowledge Graph Creation](https://shs.hal.science/hal-05484188v1): Knowledge graph creation for European mountain literary tourism research
- [Legitimation Strategies in the Foie Gras Industry](https://shs.hal.science/hal-04646338v1): Study of legitimation strategies in controversial foie gras industry by Claes et al.
